subject: Clarifying DPA notification routing and exception checklist
messages:
From: Emily Dawson <emily.dawson@clearwater-fin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearwater-fin.com
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential data exposure — initial flag and DPA obligations

Hi Kimberly,

We noticed irregular access patterns tied to traffic originating from one of your inference endpoints that handles our tenant data. Our security team has placed this into an internal investigation and asked us to trigger your DPA incident notification so we can coordinate.

At a minimum we need:
- Confirmation you received this and an initial point of contact for evidence handover.
- What your DPA defines as the notification window (we have a 72-hour statutory window we are tracking).
- Whether Redwood will supply a packaged export of impacted records and a manifest we can validate.

We are preparing a short summary and can share an encrypted forensic timeline. For now:
- Affected tenant: Clearwater Financial (account id: CLW-9932)
- Observed: unusual read throughput to historical embeddings store ~2024-06-12 22:40 UTC

Please advise next steps and who on your side will be the liaison.

Thanks,
Emily Dawson
Security Incident Response
Clearwater Financial
[attachment: initial_incident_summary.txt (text/plain)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Dawson <emily.dawson@clearwater-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2024 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial flag and DPA obligations

Thanks Emily — we received this. Looping in Ben (infra/ops) and Marissa (legal) to coordinate evidence and notification obligations.

High-level response plan from our side:
1) Acknowledge & liaise: Ben to be primary operational POC for forensics intake.
2) Triage & scope: we will validate tenant-scoped logs and confirm whether this is an exposure or anomalous access (aiming for an initial triage within 24 hours).
3) Evidence package: if exposure confirmed, we will prepare an export manifest + MD5 checksums and provide a temporary secure transfer (SFTP + signed URL).
4) Notification & timing: our default DPA notification window is 72 hours from confirmed incident; we treat the 72-hour statutory clock as starting on confirmation, not on initial flag, but we will accelerate if legal advises otherwise.

Ben — can you confirm operational capacity for evidence export and an estimated ETA for the manifest? Also call out any subprocessor involvement (e.g., third-party storage or analytics) that would change routing.

Marissa — please confirm whether we have any contractual exceptions with Clearwater (SLA/SLA exceptions, escrow commitments) that require us to escalate to execs or change the routing.

I will keep Emily updated and create a shared folder for artifacts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
[signature]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Dawson <emily.dawson@clearwater-fin.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2024 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial flag and DPA obligations

On Thu, 13 Jun 2024 10:02:00 -0700 Kimberly Park wrote:
> Ben — can you confirm operational capacity for evidence export and an estimated ETA for the manifest?

Quick ops update / checklist:
- Triage complete: isolated anomalous access to embeddings store — appears to be an index misroute, not an unbounded exfil. Scope: ~14k rows potentially impacted, tenant-specific keys present.
- Subprocessors: object storage provider (ThirdWave Storage) and our telemetry/analytics provider (SignalMesh) show no independent access beyond our service account; we'll include signed attestations from both.
- Evidence package: preparing: forensic_summary.pdf (high-level), evidence_export_manifest.csv (file list + checksums), raw request logs (redacted for other tenants).
- Transfer method: encrypted SFTP + expiring signed URLs; ETA for manifest & forensic_summary: 36 hours (EOD 2024-06-15 PDT).
- Notification timing: ops recommends confirmation = when manifest is generated and we validate integrity; that puts formal notification inside 48 hours from now if we keep this timeline.

Operational asks for Clearwater:
1) Confirm preferred transfer method (SFTP host + public SSH key) or accept signed URL.
2) If legal requires immediate notification before manifest, we will issue a preliminary notification stating we are investigating and reserve the detailed evidence handover until the manifest.

Adding Karthik for cross-border considerations — the object store is multi-region; if we need to export data containing EEA subject records, we'll follow our EU export checklist.

- Ben
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[attachment: forensic_summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Emily Dawson <emily.dawson@clearwater-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2024 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial flag and DPA obligations

Kim, Ben — thank you. Emily — thanks for flagging and for sharing the initial summary. Below are legal points and an exception-routing checklist we will follow before any formal customer notice: 

Legal & routing checklist (to be documented in the incident record):
- Confirmed scope: ops to produce manifest & checksum; Legal will review manifest for PII/regulated-data markers. We will not share raw exports that contain unrelated tenant data.
- Notification clock: per our DPA, Redwood's contractual notification is 72 hours from confirmation of a security incident that affects Clearwater data. We will treat Ben's manifest completion as the confirmation event unless evidence shows pre-confirmation notice is required by statute — in that case we will issue a preliminary notification and note that a fuller package is forthcoming.
- Subprocessor coordination: obtain signed attestations from ThirdWave Storage and SignalMesh confirming they did not access data independently and provide their own export manifests if requested. That will live in the evidence folder.
- Cross-border transfers: if manifest contains EEA personal data, we will route transfer via our EU-secure export path and log the transfer in our access audit. Karthik — please prepare the EU export checklist and confirm any SCCs or local process we must trigger.
- Exec escalation exceptions: if Clearwater requests immediate escrow or long-term custody of exported data, this requires VP-level approval and explicit contractual amendment. Do not commit to escrow without Legal/Sales leadership sign-off.
- Communication plan: ops prepares the manifest and evidence package; Legal drafts a preliminary notification for review; Sales (Kimberly) will coordinate timing and customer-facing language.

Emily — can you confirm whether Clearwater requires we open a formal JIRA ticket on your side (we can include the JIRA-INC-4872 reference) and whether you prefer SFTP or signed URL for the transfer? Also let us know if you require a notarized attestation from our subprocessors.

Once we have Ben's manifest and Karthik's EU checklist, we'll aim to provide the formal notification text within the 72-hour window.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[signature]
